# GPN change-log

## 2026-10-21 22:4x PT — **local node dashboard + Idle mode** (`gpn-agent::idle`, `gpn-agent::gui`, `gpn_node --gui`, miner park, provider claim gate)
**WHY:** a node lives on a gaming PC. Owners need to give the GPU back for a few hours without turning the node off and without dropping off the network. Requirement: idle **up to 6 h** — stop mining **and** stop AI work, keep syncing/peering/serving, then catch up and resume automatically, plus a manual resume.
**WHAT:**
* **`gpn-agent/src/idle.rs`** — the state machine. `~/.gpn/idle.json` (`{"until","reason","started"}`, **0600**, `GPN_IDLE_FILE` override) is the whole state, so idle survives a crash/reboot. `now < until` ⇒ idle, **inclusive** deadline; an expired/corrupt/missing file reads as *active* (a node that was off past the deadline starts mining). `validate_minutes` **rejects** 0 and >360 with a message naming the 6 h ceiling; `clamp_minutes` clamps config values. `claims_allowed()` is the providers' gate; `refusal_reason(peers, force)` is the sole-authority valve.
* **`gpn-agent/src/gui.rs` + `gui/index.html`** — `tiny_http` (already a dep) on **`127.0.0.1:8099`**, single embedded page (`include_str!`, no CDN, no build). `GET /api/status`, `POST /api/idle {minutes,reason}`, `POST /api/resume`; 200/400/404/405/**409** shapes. Non-loopback binds are **refused at bind time** (`0.0.0.0`, LAN IP, hostname) — the panel can stop the miner, so it is never network-reachable. Dark theme matching gpncoin.ai, labelled/keyboard-accessible, wraps to phone width.
* **Supervisor** (`gpn_node`): `--gui` / `GPN_GUI=1`, `--gui-listen` / `GPN_GUI_LISTEN`, `--force-idle` / `GPN_IDLE_FORCE=1`; one startup hint line when the GUI is off; idle reported in the startup banner; a dashboard bind failure is a warning, never a node failure. New verbs **`gpn_node idle <minutes>`** (exit 2 bad duration, 3 refused) and **`gpn_node resume`**, answered on a plain thread before the update/ollama gates (blocking reqwest must not run inside the tokio runtime — found by smoke test, panic fixed).
* **Miner** (`gpn-node` `service.rs`): `park_reason()` = idle → ai-job → none, checked each 500 ms loop; the thread parks instead of exiting, so resume needs no restart or DAG rebuild. `ParkLog` emits **one line per transition** (never per poll): `idle ended, resuming mining`. `mining_allowed(role, idle)` keeps the existing `miner_should_run` role gate authoritative — idle only ever removes permission. Idle at startup logs a loud `IDLE MODE is in force … miner starts PARKED`.
* **Providers** (`gpn_llm_provider`, `gpn_diffusion_provider`, `gpn_ml_provider`, `gpn_finetune_provider`): no new claims while idle. The LLM gate sits after the reconcile pass, so a stranded `AwaitingVerification` job is still driven terminal — idle never wedges escrow. A job is claimed **and** run inside one pass, so nothing is cut in half.
* **Windows:** `gpn-agent/windows/gpn-dashboard.cmd` (idempotent `tasklist` check → `gpn_node.exe --gui` → opens the page). `.lnk` left to the user (Send to → Desktop).
**TESTS (40 new, all green):** `idle` 14 (round-trip, 0600, 6 h ceiling/zero/over-long with the ceiling in the message, clamp, boundary just-before/at/after, restart-with-expired = active, corrupt/missing = active, claims gate, valve), `gui` 12 (routes, 200/400/404/405/409, loopback refusal, real socket round-trip + stop, no external asset), `tests/idle_mode.rs` 6 (public-API machine, HTTP end-to-end, lone-authority 409 + force, non-loopback refusal), `service::idle_mode_tests` 4, `gpn_node` `idle_cli_tests` 4. Also `cargo test --lib` 328 green and every touched bin. Smoke-tested the real binary: `idle 5` → file written 0600, `resume` clears, `idle 600` → refused, refusal path honours live peers (`system_health peers=2` on this host).
**DOCS:** `docs/node-gui-and-idle.md` (new — semantics table, valve, endpoints, CLI, config, troubleshooting) + a section in `docs/run-a-node.md` + `--help` text.
**NOT DONE (deliberate):** no binaries deployed, no live service restarted, `earnings_today` is `null` (per-block reward accounting is not tracked off-chain — an indexer/explorer decision for Jeremy).

## 2026-10-21 15:3x PT — **provider addresses are actually publishable, models are VRAM-gated, `/v1/models` is a real catalogue** (`gpn_provider_status`, `gpn_scheduler`, `gpn_llm_provider`, `gpn_node`, `gpn-agent::models`)
**WHY (four live symptoms):** (1) box2's `/status` published `listen_addrs: ["/ip4/127.0.0.1/tcp/30333/p2p/12D3…/p2p/12D3…", …]` and `multiaddrs: []` — the node RPC now returns listen addresses *already* carrying `/p2p/<id>` and litep2p sometimes doubles it; the heartbeat relayed that verbatim and the access point's sanitizer (correctly: exactly one `/p2p/<id>`, last, matching `peer_id`) rejected every entry, so the box was unroutable. (2) With no `GPN_PUBLIC_ADDR`, a NATed box published nothing and said nothing. (3) a provider advertised/claimed models its VRAM cannot hold (a 4 GB card offering `qwen2.5:7b`). (4) `/v1/models` listed `stories260K` and `tuned-…` fine-tune artifacts. (5) box2 reports `gflops: 0` with no explanation, and `list_claimable_jobs`'s `min_gflops` filter then silently hides every gated job.
**WHAT:**
* **Emitter fix** (`gpn_provider_status`): every `system_localListenAddresses` entry is normalised to `<proto>/<host>/tcp/<port>` (identity stripped, deduped) before publication; `/p2p/<peer_id>` is appended exactly once by us. `listen_addrs` is diagnostic and never carries `/p2p/`; the doubled upstream form is logged once. New `address_source` field says which rung produced `multiaddrs` (`GPN_PUBLIC_ADDR` | `node-dialability-state` | `public-listen-address` | `stun-mapped-address` | `none`).
* **Dialability ladder** in the heartbeat, mirroring the node's gate: explicit `GPN_PUBLIC_ADDR` → the node's state file (`GPN_DIALABILITY_STATE`, default `~/.gpn/dialability.json`, now written by `gpn-node` after the gate has evidence) → a public listen address → a STUN mapping **on the listen port** (new ~90-line STUN binding client, `GPN_STUN=off`, `GPN_STUN_SERVER`). Private/CGNAT/loopback/link-local/ULA ranges are never published. When nothing qualifies, `multiaddrs: []` plus a per-rung explanation and the exact fix line.
* **VRAM gating** (new `gpn-agent/src/models.rs`): size table (0.4–9.0 GB for the models we ship), 1.15× headroom, `GPN_MODEL_VRAM_HEADROOM`, `GPN_MODEL_VRAM_OVERRIDE` (`model`, `model=GB`, or `all`). Applied to `/status models[]`, to the provider's `resolve_model` claim/inference path, and to the AP's `pick()` (a provider whose VRAM can't hold the requested model is no longer routable for it). Logs `skipping <model>: needs ~X GB, node has Y GB`.
* **Public catalogue**: one shared `filter_public_models` for `/v1/models`; 16-entry assistant-grade allowlist (prefix-matched, so quant tags work), hard exclusions for `tuned-*`, `stories*`/`<0.3B` params and `*embed*`/`*rerank*`, `GPN_PUBLIC_MODELS` (CSV or `all`) to override. Excluded models stay usable when named explicitly — the catalogue is a shop window, not a permission system.
* **gflops=0** — three loud diagnostics instead of silence: the agent logs `GPU compute measurement FAILED (<reason>) — attesting gflops=0`, a once-per-process `attested compute is 0 GFLOPS — every job with min_gflops > 0 will be skipped`, a once-a-minute `[marketplace] skipping N pending job(s) …` from `list_claimable_jobs`, and a heartbeat startup warning naming both causes.
* **Shared peer id** (item 6): the supervisor now supports `GPN_NODE_KEY_FILE` / `node_key_file` and warns loudly when started with the fleet template's shared node key (`4ecac9dd…`) — the reason box2 has this box's `peer_id`. Docs give the `key generate-node-key` + restart sequence.
**TESTS:** `cargo test --bins --lib` on `gpn-agent` — 302 lib + 1 main + all bins green, incl. **12 new** in `models` (table, headroom, quant-tag match, params parser, override forms, catalogue exclusions, order/dedup), **10 new** in `gpn_provider_status` (round-trip: every emitted multiaddr passes `seedlist::clean_published_multiaddr`; the doubled form is rejected; single-suffix collapse; every private range filtered; ladder precedence; empty publication with reasons; VRAM inventory filter), **2 new** in `gpn_scheduler` (VRAM model gate in `pick`, catalogue filter). The AP's sanitizer was moved to `gpn_agent::seedlist::clean_published_multiaddr` (one definition, both sides) — `clean_p2p_multiaddr` delegates to it. `cargo check -p gpn-node` clean.
**VERIFIED LIVE (mock node RPC, real binary):** doubled-suffix box2 shape → `multiaddrs: ["/ip4/142.129.54.88/tcp/30333/p2p/12D3Koo…"]`, `address_source: GPN_PUBLIC_ADDR`, clean `listen_addrs`; same RPC without `GPN_PUBLIC_ADDR` → `multiaddrs: []` + the four-rung explanation; with a `GPN_DIALABILITY_STATE` file → `multiaddrs: ["/ip4/198.51.100.9/tcp/30333/p2p/…"]`, `address_source: node-dialability-state`. VRAM gate dropped `deepseek-r1:14b` on an 8188 MiB box in the live `/status`.
**DOCS:** `docs/provider-address-and-models.md` (new), `docs/run-a-node.md` (state-file + key-file env rows and a cross-link).
**NOTE:** `run-fleet.sh` on THIS host still pins `GPN_NODE_KEY=4ecac9dd…`; that is intentional here (single authority) and unchanged. `GPN_PUBLIC_ADDR` is still the top override, so this host's published address is unchanged.

## 2026-10-21 14:4x PT — **AP auth token is now generated on first boot** (`gpn-agent/src/ap_token.rs`)
**WHY:** the access point has required `Authorization: Bearer <GPN_AP_TOKEN>` from non-loopback callers since 2026-10, but nothing ever *produced* that token — it existed only if an operator hand-rolled one into `~/.gpn/accesspoint.env`. An install that skipped that step ran a public job API with an empty token, i.e. the non-loopback gate was silently off, and nothing in the startup log said so.
**WHAT:** new `gpn_agent::ap_token` module, called once from `gpn_scheduler::main`. Precedence is env var > env file (`$GPN_AP_TOKEN_FILE`, default `~/.gpn/accesspoint.env`) > **generated**. Generation = 24 `getrandom` bytes → 48 lowercase hex (the format hand-rolled tokens use), persisted atomically (temp + rename) at mode 0600 with the file's other variables preserved (the `GPN_AP_TOKEN=` line is replaced in place, appended if absent; `~/.gpn` created at 0700 if missing). The full value is printed **exactly once**, with the instruction to set it as the Worker's `AP_TOKEN` secret (or run `scripts/set-ap-token.sh`); later boots print `AP token loaded from <file> (first8…)` — never the full value, and a token of ≤8 chars is logged by length only. An explicitly supplied token is never overwritten and the file is not touched. A missing/unreadable/unparseable file never fails startup: since `resolve()` returns a `Result`-free `Resolved`, a corrupt (non-UTF-8 / NUL-bearing) file is quarantined to `accesspoint.env.corrupt.<epoch>` instead of being shredded, and an unwritable path degrades to an EPHEMERAL token with a loud warning.
**TESTS:** `gpn-agent/tests/ap_token.rs` — 16 integration tests (generate-when-absent + charset/length, 0600 + 0700 dir + no temp leftovers, other vars preserved, no-trailing-newline append, duplicate lines collapse, second/third boot reuse + never print the full value, env wins and leaves the file byte-identical, empty/whitespace/partial `GPN_AP_TOKEN` lines, invalid UTF-8 quarantined with original bytes intact, NUL garbage, path-is-a-directory → ephemeral, CRLF) + 2 unit tests in-module (token shape, env-line parsing). 18/18 green; `cargo build --bin gpn_scheduler` clean.
**DOCS:** `docs/run-a-node.md` (new "Auth token — generated on the first boot" subsection + `GPN_AP_TOKEN`/`GPN_AP_TOKEN_FILE` in the env table; HTML regenerated — the committed `website/docs/run-a-node.html` was ~600 lines stale), `docs/GPN-MASTER-REFERENCE.md` §6.3, `install-accesspoint.sh` (header + post-install output), `scripts/set-ap-token.sh` header, `website/deploy.html`, `website/access-points.html`.
**NOTE:** the generated token is local to this AP. The Worker at gpncoin.ai keeps its existing `AP_TOKEN` secret, so the current deployment is unaffected — only a *fresh* install needs the printed value copied over.

## 2026-10-18 05:36 PT / 12:36 UTC — PM07 GPN debug (cron 1a4f19ab) — item **#36**: stale RPC socket on the fast submitter surfaced as a **user-visible failed request**; fixed with one bounded reconnect-and-retry
**SYMPTOM:** `POST :8092/v1/chat/completions` returned `[gpn error] could not create job: Rpc error: RPC error: The background task closed connection closed; restart required` (e2e 45 s). AP journal had exactly **1** `[create] create_job submit rejected` in 48 h, at 05:29:36 — first ever of this class.
**ROOT CAUSE (evidence, not guessed):** the string is `jsonrpsee-core`'s `RestartNeeded` (`client/error.rs:43`: "The background task closed {0}; restart required") — i.e. the **WS client's background task had ended**, not a chain rejection. `ChainClient` caches one process-shared `NonceStream` with a long-lived WS client; the previous submit was 05:16:44 and the next 05:29:36 (**12.8 min idle**), so the socket was dead when the create arrived. `submit_fast_nonce` only dropped the stream *after* propagating the error, so the failure reached the user and only the **next** request (which rebuilt the stream) succeeded — confirmed: my immediate retry served in 2.29 s with no intervention, chain healthy throughout (fleet importing #152820–152843, 1 peer). Same class hit the provider one burst later (`pipelined claim #5340 failed: ... restart required` at 05:31:05); its claim loop retried and served it, but it cost a wasted burst.
**FIX (one place, `gpn-agent/src/chain/mod.rs`):** new `is_connection_lost()` (matches "restart required"/"background task closed"/"connection closed"/"not connected"/"disconnected"/"broken pipe"); `submit_fast_nonce` now wraps the submit in a loop that, on a connection-level error, drops the stale stream and **rebuilds + resubmits exactly once** (guarded by `reconnected`, `log::warn!` + stdout line). Semantics unchanged: still pool-ack, no inclusion wait; fast path flags untouched (`GPN_FAST_CLAIM=1`/`GPN_FAST_AP=1` still ON, provider logs `fast claim path: ON`). Rollback copies kept (`~/.local/bin/*.bak-20261018`).
**VERIFIED LIVE:** built + installed both bins (`84ddb5f`), restarted `gpn-accesspoint` then `gpn-provider` (all 3 units active). Requests post-deploy: 1.67 s / 3.74 s e2e (first request after restart 8.3 s = cold NonceStream build). 3 claims / 3 jobs (1:1, no storm), **0** errors/failed lines since restart, `/jobs` = 256/256 Completed, **0 Pending orphans** (#5340–#5343 healed through normally).
**RESIDUAL:** the stale-socket window itself (no client keepalive/ping on the cached WS) remains — a future idle-gap will still burn one reconnect, but no longer a failed request.

## 2026-10-16 21:56 PT / 04:56 UTC — FINDING (monitor, **report-only, no code change**): first-ever `1014 Priority is too low (2424 vs 2424)` on the AP `create_job_fast` path; **self-recovered**, root-caused to head-nonce re-seed vs pooled tx
**EVIDENCE:** `POST :8092/v1/chat/completions` at 21:56:12 returned `[gpn error] could not create job: Rpc error: ErrorObject { code: ServerError(1014), message: "Priority is too low: (2424 vs 2424)" }` (e2e 2.06 s, job 4933 not created). AP journal shows exactly **1** `[create]` rejection in 12 h; no other anomaly in-window: 12 claims / 30 min (1 per request, no storm), `/jobs` = 256 Completed / **0 Pending orphans** (4900s–4933 all Completed), `author_pendingExtrinsics` drains 1→0 every block, chain healthy (`system_health` peers=1, syncing=false; best #146015→#146018 at ~13–15 s/block — the earlier "frozen height" was just my 12 s sampling vs a 15 s cadence, **not** a stall). **Retry 50 s later succeeded in 0.72 s** (job 4933 Completed, correct `retry-ok` output) with no intervention.
**ROOT CAUSE (code-read, `gpn-agent/src/chain/{signer.rs,mod.rs}`):** the AP signs `create_job` from the shared `NonceStream`, whose nonce is seeded from the **head block** account nonce (`NonceStream::new` → `current_nonce`). `submit_fast` **drops** the stream on any submit error (and also on a runtime `spec_version` change); the next submit therefore re-seeds from head — which excludes txs still sitting in the **pool**. With ~13–18 s blocks and pool-ack-only submits, an earlier create of our own can still be pool-pending at that nonce ⇒ the re-seeded stream replays an occupied nonce at an **identical tip** ⇒ Substrate's replacement rule needs *strictly* higher priority ⇒ 1014. `_create_guard` serializes creates, so the occupying tx is ours, not a foreign signer. Recovery is exactly one block: the stream was dropped on the error, and once the pooled tx landed the reseed produced a free nonce (hence the clean 0.72 s retry).
**PROPOSED FIX (NOT applied — touches the approved fast path; wants Jeremy's OK):** in `NonceStream::submit`, treat 1014/"Priority is too low" as *"our nonce is already occupied"* → advance `next_nonce` past it and retry **once** (keep the stream, bounded), instead of dropping the stream and replaying the occupied nonce from head; equivalently seed `next_nonce` from the **pool-aware** next index (`author_pendingExtrinsics` / `system_accountNextIndex`) rather than the head nonce. Also worth one line of `println!` on the fast-submit error in `submit_fast` (env_logger defaults to ERROR, so the existing `log::warn!` re-seed line is invisible in the unit journal — this is why the triggering reseed left no trace).
**RISK if left:** ~1 request in 12 h fails with a user-visible GPN error and recovers on retry; no state corruption, no orphan, no nonce gap observed.

## 2026-10-16 21:5x PT / 04:5x UTC — PM07 driver (cron d496e0b0) — item **#30 fast-path heal churn** ROOT-CAUSED + FIXED + live-verified (off-chain; no genesis/runtime)
**Finding (class: off-chain self-amplifying churn + silent failure):** the monitor crons logged it three times today and left it unapplied — 62 `healed leaked Pending` lines across 18 ids in one hour (up to **11×** on #4884), each heal a full 4-tx burst. Two defects in `gpn_llm_provider.rs`:
1. the heal branch re-fired `accept → start → submit_result → complete` on **every 10 s reconcile tick**, but `submit_fast` is **pool-ack only** (`chain/mod.rs::submit_fast` never checks inclusion): a burst broadcast before its predecessors are included cannot land as a unit ⇒ the job is still `Pending` next tick ⇒ the whole burst is re-fired. Each retry also takes fresh nonces from the shared `NonceStream`, running it ahead of the chain and churning the pool (~240 wasted extrinsics/h) — feeding the already-escalated nonce/inclusion class.
2. `if a.is_ok() && s.is_ok() && r.is_ok() && c.is_ok() { log }` had **no `else`** ⇒ any failing leg, and the retry itself, was silent (62 attempts, zero error lines — exactly what the monitors reported).
**Fix (smallest correct change, one file, no new deps):**
- `heal_step_for_state()` — the heal path now mirrors the real state machine and submits **one** transition per tick (`Pending→accept`, `Accepted→start`, `Running→submit_result`, `AwaitingVerification→complete`, terminal/unknown→`Wait`), so a tick costs ≤1 extrinsic instead of 4.
- `heal_attempt_allowed()` + `HEAL_RETRY_COOLDOWN = 45 s` — per-`(job, step)` throttle (≈2–3 block intervals at the current cadence) so a retry cannot allocate a new nonce inside one inclusion window; entries are dropped on terminal states (`heal_forget`) to keep the map bounded.
- every leg now logs: benign `JobNotPending`/`JobNotAccepted` races stay quiet, real failures `eprintln!`.
- **bonus correctness:** a leaked job that reaches `Accepted` with an off-chain result is now *started* (next tick submits the result → provider paid per token) instead of taking the result-less zombie path (start+complete = full refund).
**Tests:** +3 (`heal_walks_one_transition_per_tick`, `heal_ignores_terminal_and_unknown_states`, `heal_gate_admits_one_attempt_per_cooldown`) — `cargo test --release --bin gpn_llm_provider` **7/7 green**; release bin builds clean.
**Live (rule 5a):** new binary installed to `~/.local/bin` (`.bak` kept), `systemctl --user restart gpn-provider` (accesspoint + heartbeat + provider active, `fast claim path: ON`). **Before** (same journal, old binary): #4927 healed 4× in 40 s, #4931 healed accept 5× in 60 s. **After** (21:51:28 →, 1 job served): `POST :8092/jobs` → **#4932 claimed → inferred → result returned → Completed** with **exactly one** heal line in the entire window (`heal #4932: accept submitted (Pending)` — the benign late-arrival accept). No repeats, no silent legs. Canonical genesis WASM untouched; no `set_code`.
**Residual (separate, escalated — NOT this item):** the ~18 s block cadence / authoring stalls (single-peer topology + duplicate-block-request ban loop, see 19:5x entry) that make inclusion slow enough for a leak to occur at all, and the AP label-vs-`NextJobId` +drift.

## 2026-10-15 14:47 PT / 21:47 UTC — FIX: `gpn_node` **legacy-DB pruning guard missed the box-#1 DB** → node crash-looped (`Incompatible pruning modes`). Now pins a base path, detects the OS-default DB, and never forces `archive` on an unknown DB.
**PROBLEM (box #1, real, live):** `gpn_node` launched its `gpn-node` child with `--state-pruning archive --blocks-pruning archive` (the sync-robustness defaults) while the on-disk DB was a legacy `--state-pruning 256` one → the child died instantly, every 30s:
`Error: Service(Client(StateDatabase("Incompatible pruning modes [stored: Constrained { max_blocks: Some(256) }; requested: ArchiveAll]")))` → `[supervisor] node: exited (exit code 1) after 0s — restarting in 30000ms`. **Root cause:** the commit-a93d379 guard decided "fresh vs existing DB" from a base path that was only read from `GPN_BASE_PATH`/config `base_path` — and box #1 sets **neither**. With no `--base-path`, `gpn_node` passed none to the node, so the node used the **OS-default** dir `%LOCALAPPDATA%\gpn-node.exe\data` (where the legacy DB actually lives) while the guard inspected `None` → `existing_db(None) == false` → forced `archive` onto the legacy DB → instant crash-loop. The check and the node disagreed about which directory they were talking about.
**FIX (no genesis change, no runtime-WASM regen, no `set_code`):**
- **`gpn-agent/src/bin/gpn_node.rs` — pinned base path.** New resolution `GPN_BASE_PATH` → config `base_path` → default `C:\gpn\data` (Windows) / `~/.gpn/node` (Unix). That single path is now used **both** for the DB-existence check **and** the node's `--base-path` (always passed), so the guard can never inspect a different dir than the node. Backward-compat: if the pinned path has no DB but the **OS-default** path does (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\gpn-node.exe\data`), the OS-default DB is auto-detected and used (with a warning) — so an existing box keeps its chain instead of silently starting fresh.
- **Robust pruning guard.** New `pruning_plan()`: fresh dir → `--state-pruning archive --blocks-pruning archive` (+ drops a `.gpn-pruning-archive` marker); existing DB **with** our marker → archive (safe, we created it); existing **legacy/unknown** DB → request **no** pruning flags (fall back to the node's compiled defaults, which match the stored mode) + a clear warning. Explicit `GPN_NODE_ARGS`/`node_args` pruning flags always win. The node can no longer crash-loop on `Incompatible pruning modes`.
- **`gpn-agent/src/bin/gpn_snapshot.rs`.** `export` records the source DB's pruning mode in the manifest (`pruning`); `import` re-materialises it as the same `.gpn-pruning-archive` marker — so an imported **archive** snapshot is correctly archive-flaggable by `gpn_node` (a legacy/unknown snapshot stays unmarked → left alone, safe).
- **`.github/workflows/release-windows.yml`** — generated `C:\gpn\start-node.cmd` now sets `GPN_BASE_PATH=C:\gpn\data` (consistent with the pinned default; legacy localappdata DB still auto-detected).
- **Docs** — `docs/run-a-node.md` (pinned base path + legacy-DB caveat + migration: wipe `chains/` or import the archive snapshot) and `docs/fast-sync.md` (marker round-trip, Windows base-path note).
**VERIFY (Linux):** `cargo test --bin gpn_node` → **7/7 green** (`fresh_dir_requests_archive`, `legacy_db_is_left_alone`, `marked_archive_db_keeps_archive`, `explicit_node_args_respected`, `legacy_os_default_db_is_detected`, `pinned_db_wins_over_empty_legacy`, `default_base_path_is_pinned`); `cargo check --bins` clean.

Root host fix needs `sudo resolvectl dns enp42s0 1.1.1.1 192.168.1.1 && resolvectl flush-caches` (root not available), so GPN was made **robust to it** app-side.
**FIX (no runtime/genesis/WASM touched; no `set_code`):**
- **NEW `gpn-agent/src/net.rs`** — `Ipv4OnlyResolver` (a `reqwest::dns::Resolve` impl that does an **AF_INET-only** `getaddrinfo`, via `libc`, so **no AAAA query is ever issued**) + `ipv4_only_client(timeout)` = that resolver + a bounded `connect_timeout`. Verified `getaddrinfo(AF_INET)` = 0.0s vs `AF_UNSPEC` = 15s on the affected host.
- **Provider (`gpn_llm_provider.rs`)** — `return_result()` now POSTs with `net::ipv4_only_client(5s)`. Also honors `GPN_RESULT_URL` / `GPN_AP_URL` (base, or full `.../result`) to pin a **loopback** callback for a co-located AP (removes public-DNS entirely); precedence env > AP-advertised `callback` (remote providers unchanged).
- **AP (`gpn_scheduler.rs`)** — `dispatch_assignment()` (the `/assign` push to a provider) uses the same IPv4-only client. The advertised callback default, when `--listen` is a **wildcard** bind (`0.0.0.0`/`::`) and no `--callback-url`/`GPN_AP_CALLBACK_URL`/`GPN_PUBLIC_URL` is set, is now **loopback** (`loopback_if_wildcard`) instead of the unroutable wildcard.
- **Docs** — `docs/run-a-node.md`: new troubleshooting section “slow LLM jobs on a dual-stack / AAAA-laggy host (the `/result` stall)” (symptom, mechanism, the fix, the `GPN_RESULT_URL` loopback option, and the root `resolvectl` one-liner). New tool: `gpn-agent/examples/dns_probe.rs`.
**VERIFY (no host-DNS change):** `cargo run --example dns_probe` → `dual-stack ERROR in 8.000s` / `ipv4-only http=200 in 0.012s`. Rebuilt + installed `~/.local/bin/{gpn_llm_provider,gpn_scheduler}` + restarted the two units. Provider log now shows `[job N] result returned to AP (http://gpn-testnet.duckdns.org:8092)` (the exact previously-stalling URL). e2e text via AP `:8092` `/v1/chat/completions`: **2.2–4.3s** (was 19–22s) — **<5s cap MET**. Unit tests: `net::` 3/3, `gpn_scheduler` 19/19 (incl. new `callback_default_uses_loopback_for_wildcard_binds`) GREEN.

## 2026-10-15 12:10 PT / 19:10 UTC — CI FIX (release-windows): deploy step now a true **auto-update** (stop → copy → **restart**), node no longer left down.
**PROBLEM:** `.github/workflows/release-windows.yml` → step `deploy binaries directly to C:\gpn\bin` stopped every `gpn*` process (to free `.exe` locks) and copied the new bins, but **never restarted** them. Box #1 **IS** the GitHub self-hosted runner (`DESKTOP-USBUADL`), so **every Windows build took box #1 offline** until Jeremy manually restarted it — it had been down ~39 h since the last build.
**FIX (one step, no runtime/genesis/WASM touched):** renamed to `deploy binaries + restart node … (auto-update)` and made it a clean **stop → copy → restart**: (0) (re)write `C:\gpn\start-node.cmd` — the idempotent config file — with chain `C:\gpn\testnet-spec.json` (fallback `testnet` if absent; AP serves the spec at `/genesis-spec`, the documented way a fresh node pins the canonical genesis WASM), `GPN_RPC_PORT=9944`, `GPN_ENDPOINT=ws://gpn-testnet.duckdns.org:9944`, canonical bootnode `/dns4/gpn-testnet.duckdns.org/tcp/30333/p2p/12D3KooWAFtUNxc6RgC9rq5uSHXd5XUncEcPqp77UU98oN6hSVFo`, box #1's author/payout (`GPN_AUTHOR=bob`, `GPN_ACCOUNT=5FHneW46…`, `GPN_SIGNER=//Bob`) + `GPN_NODE_KEY`, working dir `C:\gpn`; (1) **stop** — end the supervisor task(s) + kill all `gpn*` + retire the legacy `GPNProvider` task/`run-provider.ps1` supervisor (so exactly ONE supervisor runs — two would fight over `:8094` + the DB); (2) **copy** the new bins; (3+4) **restart** via a **Scheduled Task** (`schtasks /Create /TN GPN-Node … /SC ONLOGON /RL HIGHEST` + `/Run`), plus best-effort detached `ollama serve`; then verify (process list + `:9944` `system_health`).
**WHY THE TASK SURVIVES:** the GitHub runner kills its **own** job process tree at end-of-job, so a plain `Start-Process` child dies when the job ends (that is exactly what kept box #1 down). A task launched by `schtasks /Run` is parented to the **Task Scheduler service** (`svchost`), **not** the job → it detaches from job teardown and keeps running on the box (inspectable via `schtasks /Query /TN GPN-Node`).
**GATE:** default = always (re)start; set repo variable `GPN_AUTOSTART_NODE=false` to disable. **HARD RULES honored:** no genesis change, no canonical runtime-WASM regen, no `set_code`.
**VERIFY:** YAML parses (12 steps); PowerShell here-string renders at column 0 (static review — no `pwsh`/Windows here). NOTE/residual: expects `C:\gpn\testnet-spec.json` to exist on the box (else falls back to `--chain testnet`); the deploy deletes the legacy `GPNProvider` task (re-run `windows-provider-start.yml` would recreate a second supervisor — avoid running both).

Fix: new `scripts/install-ollama.ps1` + `scripts/install-ollama.sh` (install → serve → pull baseline); `run-windows-provider.ps1` self-heals (`-InstallOllama`) or fails with exact commands; `run-windows.bat` checks/starts ollama; `install.sh` output documents it; `docs/run-a-node.md`, `website/download.html`, `website/deploy.html` document install/serve/pull. Provider pre-flights ollama (`llm::infer::ollama_reachable`) → **one** actionable warning + suppressed sentinel (no per-poll spam); `gpn_node` warns at startup that the node mines but can't serve LLMs. **Verified:** ~40 s provider run with ollama absent → exactly one warning, zero pull-failure lines.

Files: `gpn-node/node/src/{command,service}.rs`, `gpn-agent/src/bin/{gpn_node,gpn_llm_provider}.rs`, `gpn-agent/src/llm/infer.rs`, `scripts/install-ollama.{ps1,sh}`, `run-windows-provider.ps1`, `run-windows.bat`, `install.sh`, `docs/run-a-node.md`, `website/{download,deploy}.html`, `GPN-TASKS.md`.

## 2026-10-08 02:55 PT / 09:55 UTC — PM07 driver (cron d496e0b0) — item **#10 Diffusion silent-wedge instrumentation** → **DONE** (live-verified)
**What changed (one file; no chain/genesis/runtime touched):** `gpn-agent/src/bin/gpn_diffusion_provider.rs` — `run_job` used to `await` the diffusers helper via an unchecked `Command::output()`, so a hung render blocked the entire provider loop **indefinitely and silently** (the "silent wedge"; only a restart cleared it).  New `run_with_watchdog(cmd, timeout, label)`:
1. runs the helper under a **hard budget** (`GPN_DIFFUSE_TIMEOUT_SECS`; default **600 s** image / **1800 s** video);
2. emits a **30 s progress heartbeat** (`[watchdog] … still running — elapsed=Ns`) so a slow render is no longer dead air;
3. at the budget **kills the hung child** and logs `⚠ SILENT-WEDGE DETECTED` + marks the job errored off-chain (never silent);
4. a process-local `wedged` set **skips re-rendering a proven-wedge job** (avoids a tight GPU-burning retry loop); the chain-side expiry sweep reclaims it.
**Tests:** 5/5 bin tests green (success output; hung helper killed+flagged+prompt; nonzero-exit ≠ wedge; timeout defaults; wedged-marker roundtrip).

## 2026-10-07 17:52 PT / 00:52 UTC — PM07 driver (cron d496e0b0) — item **#3 Client-side RTT / user→nearest-node** → **DONE**
**What changed (smallest correct change; no chain/genesis touched):**
1. **New `gpn-agent/src/routing.rs`** — `RttOverrides` + `effective_latency_ms` (client-measured user→provider RTT wins over AP-measured, `0`/absent = fall back), `parse_rtt_overrides` (lenient; malformed/non-positive ignored, never fatal), `lookup_override` (matches by provider **address** or **status URL**, case-insensitive, `/status`+trailing-slash normalized). 5 unit tests green.

## 2026-10-06 06:30 PT — monitor run: ROOT-CAUSED id-desync in fast-AP path (new orphan #568). No code deploy this run (needs MAIN review + build).

**Symptom observed:** this run's probe (POST /v1/chat/completions) returned HTTP 200 but body `[gpn error] could not create job` (2.07s). An immediate single retry succeeded (real 425-char answer). `/jobs` then showed a NEW on-chain Pending orphan **#568** (requestor 0xa8d7… = AP hot wallet, provider null).

**Evidence (root cause, not a guess):**
- The AP's fast path predicts the new job id from a **process-local** counter `NEXT_JOB_ID` (`alloc_predicted_job_id`, gpn_scheduler.rs:106). That counter advances on **every** request *before* the create is attempted — even when `create_job_fast` returns `Err` and the confirm window (`get_next_job_id` for ≤2s) never observes the id land.
- Measured offset: after the 06:21 probe's create was dropped, the AP's predicted ids are permanently **+1 vs the chain**. Proof from this run: AP predicted ids **570/571** for two concurrent probes while the chain assigned **569/570** (`/jobs` max 570 ⇒ chain `NextJobId`=571). Earlier: AP predicted 569 → chain created 568 (AP 569 = chain 568). Before 06:21 the two matched (566/567 = 566/567).
- Consequence: AP-keyed `llm_store.json` / `assignments.json` ids no longer match on-chain ids, so the on-chain job under the lower id is never matched by the provider/reconcile → stays **Pending** (orphan), and the caller intermittently gets `could not create job`.
- Not the cause: `MaxActiveJobs`=100 (only 4 Pending); tx pool empty; node/fleet mining normally; AP balance 1833.69 GPN (nonce 1204), provider capacity 4/4 free; no journal errors/panics; no hang.

**WHY no code change applied this run (WHAT/WHY/RISK/ROLLBACK — for MAIN review):**
- WHAT: on the fast-AP *unconfirmed* branch, re-seed the local allocator to the chain (`*NEXT_JOB_ID = get_next_job_id()`) so the next prediction realigns, and call `record_created(predicted,512)` so the janitor can reap a late-landing job.
- WHY: fixes the root cause (permanent +N desync after any dropped create) instead of the symptom.
- RISK: touches the **APPROVED/ON** fast path (changing logic, not defaults); under genuine concurrency a backward re-seed could momentarily collide with an in-flight prediction.
- ROLLBACK: revert the small diff; fast path otherwise unchanged.
- Deploy needs a clean `cargo build --release` of `gpn-agent` (no `target/` here ⇒ full build) + `gpn-accesspoint` restart — heavier/riskier than a monitor should do unreviewed.
- **Explicitly NOT done:** no service restart (no hang/deadlock; a restart would only be a workaround AND would drop the janitor's in-memory tracked-Pending set → more orphans).

**Result this run:** services active (AP PID 1110762, provider PID 1098961 ~16.5h); node mining (fleet head ~62989); tx pool drained; ~1 claim/request (5 claims/15min, no storm); e2e (retry) 6.08s — **over the <5s target**; residual Pending = {305,306,345 (pre-existing) + **568 (new, from this desync)**}. Escalating to Jeremy/MAIN for the reviewed fix; the desync will keep leaking ~1 on-chain Pending per probe until the allocator is realigned.

## 2026-10-07 14:45 PT / 21:45 UTC — GPN queue driver (item 1, step 2) — provider advertises `/status` endpoint ON-CHAIN; root-caused the "variant doesn't exist" txpool rejection; LIVE-VERIFIED

On-chain metadata already had call_index 10; the node just couldn't decode it.
**Fix (smallest correct):** rebuilt `gpn-node` (runtime `build.rs` embeds the committed canonical WASM via `include_bytes!`, so genesis is untouched) and restarted `gpn-fleet`. Restarted dependents (`gpn-accesspoint`/`gpn-diffusion`/`gpn-provider-heartbeat`/`gpn-provider`) per the post-upgrade rule. TEXT e2e via AP :8092 → HTTP 200 "ENDPOINT-OK" (#1102) **5.83s**; NextJobId advanced ⇒ create path healthy.

(b) minor/cosmetic: `submit_signed` logged a FALSE `ProviderNotRegistered` for the call that actually succeeded (mis-attribution when `our_index` can't be resolved against the block) — on-chain effect was correct; follow-up.

## 2026-10-08 03:20 UTC / 2026-10-07 20:20 PT — GPN queue driver (item 5b, video gen) — **alias bug FIXED; item BLOCKED on hardware (T5-XXL)**
**Item 5b (exercise + verify video generation / ltx-video)** — first TODO after 2/4 BLOCKED, 1/3/5a DONE.
**Root-caused before acting:** ran the helper directly. Found a real bug: `gpn_diffuse.py::model_id()` resolved image aliases (`sd-turbo`…) but **not the video aliases**, so the default/`auto` video model passed the literal string `"ltx-video"` to `LTXPipeline.from_pretrained()` → guaranteed failure `OSError: Cannot load model ltx-video`. (The provider's `ensure_model` mapped it for *downloading*, but the helper that actually builds the pipeline did not.)
**Fix (commit `19536de`):** `model_id(m, kind)` now maps `ltx-video`/`ltx`/`auto`→`Lightricks/LTX-Video` (unit-checked). Added a memory-fitting load path in `gen_video`: on small GPUs (<10 GB total) auto-load an **NF4 4-bit T5 pinned to CPU** (`device_map={'':'cpu'}`) and move only the small transformer+VAE to the GPU, + VAE tiling/slicing. Big GPUs keep the exact prior unquantized path. Env override `GPN_DIFFUSE_T5_4BIT={auto,1,0}`. Installed `bitsandbytes 0.50.2` (PyPI; py3.12/cu124).
**Blocked — hardware (empirical):** LTX-Video's cost is its **T5-XXL** text encoder (~18 GB fp32 / ~22 GB fp16); the 2B transformer is only ~7 MB fp32 (7.2 GB). Two cgroup-isolated attempts (MemoryMax 8–11G, `--user --scope`, so the node was never at risk):
  - naive `.to("cuda")` → `CUDA OOM: tried to allocate 5.93 GiB, 4.47 GiB free` (node 1.09 GB + ollama 1.52 GB already hold VRAM);
  - 4-bit T5 `device_map=cpu` → scope **OOM-killed** after ~3 min (bnb must stage the fp32 shards, ≈18 GB, to quantize → exceeds this host's 15 GB RAM, ~5.4 GB free).
⇒ This host (RTX 4060 **8 GB VRAM / 15 GB RAM**) cannot render LTX-Video at any quantization; matches the 2026-09-03 note + USE-GPN §4.3. **No chain/genesis/runtime change. No restart.** Node untouched (verified: cgroup isolated, best # advancing). **Next (needs a bigger host):** render on ≥16 GB VRAM + ≥32 GB RAM, or add a pre-quantized (GGUF) T5 loader / a lighter video model. Docs updated (USE-GPN §4.3, GPN-TASKS 5b). **NOTE:** the helper has no `Command` timeout in the provider → a genuinely-hanging gen would wedge the diffusion lane (item 10 scope).

## 2026-10-08 00:47 UTC — PM07 driver (cron d496e0b0) — item **#9b janitor → pallet `expire_job`** → **DONE (live-verified)**
**Root cause:** the AP stale-job janitor could only reclaim its **own still-`Pending`** jobs via requestor-side `cancel_job`; the pallet's **permissionless `expire_job`** (live since spec 7/8) was never called. So provider-abandoned `Accepted`/`Running` orphans, and orphans lost from the in-memory list across an AP restart, held a global `ActiveJobCount` slot forever.
**Fix (`bee8be0`, no runtime/genesis change):** `ChainClient::expire_job`/`expire_job_fast` (call_index 9; permissionless; any non-terminal state) + `get_job_timing(created_at,max_duration)`. The `gpn_scheduler` janitor now reclaims **primary** via the pallet `expire_job` for any non-terminal job past `created_at+max_duration` (also clears Accepted/Running orphans), keeps requestor `cancel_job` as the fast path for our own stale Pending jobs, and **seeds tracking from the last 256 chain job ids at startup** so a restart no longer leaks slots. Pure helpers `is_terminal_state`/`past_deadline` + 2 unit tests.
**Build/tests:** `cargo test --bin gpn_scheduler` **6/6**; `cargo test --lib` **68/68**; `cargo build --release --bin gpn_scheduler` clean.
**Live:** stopped → swapped `~/.local/bin/gpn_scheduler` → started `gpn-accesspoint`; log `[janitor] re-adopted 8 non-terminal job(s) from #1044..#1299` then all 8 **expired on-chain** via `ComputeMarketplace::expire_job` (`block 93025 > deadline …`). Fresh e2e create `#1300` (llama3.2:1b via AP :8092) → Completed. **On-chain `expire_job` confirmed working** (permissionless, from the AP account). Canonical genesis WASM untouched.
**Next:** queue's next TODO is **#9c (RPC-readiness gate)**. Items 2/6/7 spec-13 `set_code` remain gated on explicit go-ahead.

**WHAT:** Deployed the `31dc849` Windows bundle to the box and restarted its provider — `windows-provider-deploy.yml` (run `37862554157`, inputs `run_id=37856682989`) then `windows-provider-start.yml` (run `37862631897`), both **success** (self-hosted runner `DESKTOP-USBUADL` online). Then live-tested routing/claim/completion.
**WHY:** item #14's documented next step after the `31dc849` claim-filter fix was "deploy to the box → confirm a `min_vram_mb:16000` job claims **and completes** on the 5070 Ti".
**RESULT (verified live):** box now **claims** remote-assigned jobs (previously it never claimed): `POST :8092/jobs {min_vram_mb:16000, model:qwen2.5:7b}` → **#1755 routed_to `5FHneW46…` → Claimed → `Running`**; second floored job **#1756** likewise Claimed→Running; a *local* 4060 job **#1757 → Completed** (no regression). So the `31dc849` fix is confirmed live.
**ROOT CAUSE of the remaining gap (completion):** a REMOTE provider can claim but never *run/complete*. The prompt is written only into the **AP host's** `~/.gpn` LlmStore (`gpn_scheduler.rs`: `LlmStore::put(id, LlmJob::new_llm(...))` then waits on *its own* store for status `done`). The box has a **different** store (`HOME` unset ⇒ `System32\.gpn\`), and `dispatch_assignment` / `POST /assign` (served by `gpn_provider_status`) deliver only `{job_id,model,pull}` — **no prompt**. Hence the box's `run_job` has no local `get_job(id)` and both the fast-path and the main `Running` scan skip it (`if let Some(job) = get_job(id)`) ⇒ it sits `Running` until the item-9e expiry sweep reclaims it (no permanent leak).
**RISK:** low for what was done (artifact deploy + service restart, no genesis/runtime/`set_code`; canonical genesis WASM `76f37b23…` untouched). The remaining fix is NOT applied.
**ROLLBACK:** box provider binary — redeploy a prior `release-windows` run-id via `windows-provider-deploy`.
**NEXT (needs MAIN REVIEW/APPROVE — touches the AP request path):** include the prompt in the assignment and have the provider persist it into its own local LlmStore on `/assign`, and add a result-return channel back to the requesting AP. Off-chain only; no genesis/runtime change.

## 2026-10-08 21:35 PT / 04:35 UTC — PM07 GPN queue-driver (cron d496e0b0), item #16 red-team — FINDING #7 (agent/AP auth bypass) FIXED + LIVE-VERIFIED (`f0a8c55`, off-chain; no genesis/runtime)
**Finding #7:** the provider heartbeat `POST /assign` on the publicly-forwarded :8093 was **unauthenticated** — any remote caller could inject an arbitrary `LlmJob` into the provider's own store (unauthorized GPU work, no on-chain escrow) and **overwrite a pending assignment's `callback`/`callback_token`**, so the provider would POST a **user's** inference result to the attacker (**result hijack / data exfiltration**). Reproduced live: `POST /assign` → 200 with no token (local + box :8093 reachable).
**Fix:** shared AP↔provider secret. `gpn_provider_status`: new `--assign-token`/`GPN_ASSIGN_TOKEN`; `POST /assign` rejects a **non-loopback** caller whose `X-Gpn-Assign-Token` doesn't match (constant-time → 401); loopback exempt; unset token = legacy-accept + warn (non-breaking rollout). `gpn_scheduler::dispatch_assignment` sends the token (header + body). `windows-provider-start.yml` passes the repo secret to the box heartbeat. +4 tests.
**Verify (non-loopback = host LAN IP):** no token → 401, wrong → 401, correct → 200; loopback no-token → 200; e2e creates **#1820/#1821 Completed** (no regression). Token set in `~/.gpn/accesspoint.env` + `gpn-provider-heartbeat.service`; bins reinstalled; services restarted.
**Carry-forward:** set the `GPN_ASSIGN_TOKEN` GitHub secret (= AP host token) then `windows-provider-deploy`+`start` so the box enforces it (box `.exe` predates the fix → legacy until redeployed). STATUS: GREEN.

## 2026-10-09 08:5x PT — PM07 GPN queue-driver (cron d496e0b0), item #16 red-team — FINDING #27 (gpu-attestation / state consistency — non-root) FIXED + STAGED (spec 34; no genesis, not applied)
**Finding #27 (gpu-attestation, state consistency / invariant break):** `AttestedProviderCount` is incremented **only** by a *fresh* `submit_attestation`, but `deposit_stake` does NOT touch it (a stake may be deposited *before* attesting — or never attested at all). `withdraw_stake` decremented it **unconditionally** (`AttestedProviderCount::mutate(|c| c.saturating_sub(1))`), so any signed account could run `deposit_stake(min)` → `withdraw_stake()` **without ever attesting** and drive the counter below its true value — repeatable to pin it at 0. The counter is defined as the number of *attested* providers, so the withdraw-side decrement must mirror the increment side.
**Fix (smallest correct change):** capture `<Attestations<T>>::contains_key(&who)` **before** removing the record and decrement `AttestedProviderCount` **only** when it was true. +regression test `test_withdraw_without_attest_does_not_corrupt_attested_count` (a deposit-only account's withdraw leaves the count unchanged; a genuinely attested account still decrements it); `pallet-gpu-attestation` **39/39 green** (was 38).

## 2026-10-09 10:2x PT — PM07 GPN queue-driver (cron d496e0b0), item #16 red-team — FINDING #30 (compute-marketplace / payment-channel theft-of-service — non-root, permissionless) FIXED + STAGED (spec 37; no genesis, not applied)
**Finding #30 (compute-marketplace, payment-channel theft-of-service):** the finding-#20 fix added a unilateral `refund_expired_channel` so an untouched channel could not be permanently locked, guarded by `channel.nonce == 0 && channel.balance_provider == 0` to prove the provider held no co-signed claim. But those are the **on-chain** channel fields, and per `design-offchain-escrow-channels.md` the per-job money movement is entirely off-chain (open/close are the only on-chain txs) — so during a channel's whole life the on-chain `nonce` stays `0` no matter how much value moved. The guard is therefore **vacuous** (always true for an `Open` channel). A requestor could co-sign per-job updates (the provider delivers real compute, so it legitimately holds a state with `balance_provider > 0`), then stop, wait out the deadline and call `refund_expired_channel` to reclaim the **entire** deposit — the provider paid nothing for delivered work (the requestor wins the deadline race; the provider has no guaranteed first move, though a cooperative/force-close needs the counterparty sig and only unlocks at the deadline).
**Fix (smallest correct change):** a **race-free dispute window** — `refund_expired_channel` now requires `now >= channel.deadline + ChannelRefundDelay` (new `#[pallet::constant]`, runtime-wired to **300 blocks ≈ 75 min @15s**); the provider (holding the requestor-co-signed latest state) always has that window to `force_close_channel` its claim first, and a later refund then fails `ChannelNotOpen`. New `Error::ChannelWithinDisputePeriod`; path stays requestor-only and still requires `nonce == 0`/zero provider balance. +regression test `test_refund_expired_channel_blocked_during_dispute_window` (refused exactly at and one block before the window end; provider force-closes its co-signed claim mid-window and gets paid; requestor's later refund rejected); `pallet-compute-marketplace` **49/49 green** (was 48).
**Artifact (staged, NOT applied):** runtime rebuilt from HEAD with the canonical genesis WASM moved aside → built → **restored (sha `76f37b23…` intact)**; `spec_version` 36→**37**; `shared/artifacts/project7/wasm/gpn_runtime_spec37_redteam_channel_refund_window.compact.compressed.wasm` (sha `8b10e557…`; on-chain 22 ⇒ valid bump) — carries **all** spec-36 payloads (findings #1/#3/#8/#9/#10/#11/#12/#13/#14/#16/#18/#19/#20/#21/#22/#23/#25/#26/#27/#28/#29 + item-19 min-GPU floor) **plus** #30; spec-36 artifact moved to `wasm/superseded/`; `README-pending-upgrade.md` names spec-37 LATEST.
**Apply:** gated (chain-wide `set_code` = review-first), same as the spec-17…37 stack. STATUS: staged.

**Root-cause-first (evidence before action):** re-ran the standard probe + re-read the claim pipeline; **no restart, no code/env/flag/state change**. **Confirmation (mechanism pinned in code):** `read_assigned()` (`gpn_llm_provider.rs:309-338`) returns all 1732 entries matching our account; the claim loop (`:580-649`) then calls `get_job_state(id)` (~2 `storage_at_head` reads) for every id **that has no local store entry** — and only ~13 ids do (llm_store.json = 8.8 KB vs assignments.json = 220 KB). So ~1730 ids × ~2 reads ≈ **3.4k blocking subxt reads per cycle** ⇒ the observed ~28–30 s claim-to-claim period (`claiming LLM job #0` 13:22:26 → 13:22:42 → 13:23:00, ~28 s). `write_assignment()` (`gpn_scheduler.rs:701-723`) only inserts, never prunes ⇒ monotonic growth. **PROPOSAL (needs MAIN APPROVE — touches the APPROVED fast path):**
- **WHAT:** bound the claim scan + prune the store: (a) in `read_assigned`/claim loop, skip any id already terminal locally and keep a small persisted "seen/finished" set so settled ids are never re-scanned; (b) make `write_assignment` drop an entry once its job reaches a terminal off-chain state (or cap `assignments.json` to the last N unfinished assignments); (c) one-time prune of the existing ~1730 stale entries.

- **RISK:** a too-aggressive prune could drop a genuinely-unclaimed fresh assignment and stall a job. Mitigate: only prune terminal/completed entries and entries with no local payload older than a safe window; keep all `Pending` and recently-assigned ids; keep the fast path's optimistic-claim bound intact.
- **ROLLBACK:** `git revert` the commit + restart provider/AP; `assignments.json` is append-only/regenerable ⇒ no data loss.

## 2026-10-14 14:42 PT / 21:42 UTC — PM07 GPN debug (cron 95b27deb) — **SERVICE OUTAGE (job-create + on-chain discovery) after spec-41 runtime upgrade; ROOT-CAUSED + FIXED (restart) + VERIFIED.** e2e recovered 2.23s warm.
**ANOMALY FOUND:** `POST /v1/chat/completions` **hung → curl timeout 90s (no response)**; `POST /jobs` → HTTP200 `{"error":"Rpc error … ServerError(1010) … \"Invalid Transaction\" … \"Transaction is outdated\"","ok":false}`; `:8092/health` = `{"providers":1}` (baseline **3**). Provider log: `set_provider_endpoint(http://gpn-testnet.duckdns.org:8093/status) failed: … ServerError(1010) "Transaction is outdated"`.
**ROOT CAUSE (measured, not assumed):** The verifier/sudo security rotation **upgraded the runtime spec_version 40 → 41** and swapped the node binary (`gpn-node.bak-20261014-142102`, node restarted 14:21:11; commit `5aed68d` @14:23). The agent processes were restarted **at 14:21:03 — *before* the node finished coming back up** (node ready 14:21:11 one restart / 14:21:12 next). Their long-lived `OnlineClient` therefore bound **genesis-era / stale (spec-40) metadata** (`connect_best_block` fell back to `from_url`). All **head-block storage reads then fail** (subxt runtime-version/metadata mismatch): `current_nonce()` → `unwrap_or(0)` ⇒ txs submitted with **nonce 0** vs the account's real nonce (provider account nonce = **53989**) ⇒ rejected **`Transaction is outdated`** (CheckNonce *Stale*). Same failure makes `list_provider_endpoints()` return empty ⇒ `health.providers`=1. **Proof it is client-side, not chain-side:** raw RPC `state_getRuntimeVersion`/`state_getMetadata` @best all return spec **41** (len 169114); a *fresh* client (`gpn_check_state`) reads nonce fine; node mining normally (#133998+, 2 peers). Binaries do **NOT** need rebuild (they fetch metadata dynamically).
**FIX (one, targeted):** restart `gpn-provider` then `gpn-accesspoint` **after the node was up**, so the clients re-fetch best-block spec-41 metadata.
**RESULT (verified):** `:8092/health`=`{"providers":3,"status":"ok"}`; `:8093/health`=`{"status":"ok"}`; provider logs `advertised on-chain endpoint: …` (no tx error); **e2e** `POST /v1/chat/completions` → HTTP200 coherent, job **#3960** (cold, model reload, 32.4s) then **#3961 cold-warm 2.23s** (<5s cap); `GET /jobs` 256 jobs, **0 Pending**; all 5 units active.
**ROLLBACK:** none needed — restart only, **no code/state/flag change**; fast path (`GPN_FAST_CLAIM=1`/`GPN_FAST_AP=1`) untouched per DON'T-REVERT. Tree clean @`5aed68d`.
**FLAG FOR JEREMY (medium):** the spec-41 rotation (commit `5aed68d`) had this restart-ordering side effect — whenever a runtime upgrade lands, **restart the agent services *after* the node is fully up** (or the agents come back bound to genesis metadata and every create/claim/sponsor tx is rejected). Not a rotation defect; an operational ordering note. Note the runtime upgrade WAS committed (spec 41) — the earlier 13:48 change-log line "tree clean @86c1c69" is superseded.

## 2026-10-14 22:08 PT / 2026-10-15 05:08 UTC — PM07 GPN debug (cron 1a4f19ab) — serving, 0 unit ERRORs. ANOMALY: job #3998 stranded in `Running` (off-chain payload LOST); its client request hung. ROOT-CAUSED to the lock-free shared store (`llm_store.json`). NO mutating action — self-heals via the AP janitor; no hang/deadlock; fast path untouched per DON'T-REVERT.
**CHECKS:** all 5 units (`gpn-provider`/`gpn-accesspoint`/`gpn-fleet`/`gpn-fleet-directive`/`gpn-provider-heartbeat`) **active**; `gpn-provider` NRestarts=**0** (pid 3721716, up 7.5h). `:8092/health`=`{"providers":3,"status":"ok"}`, `:8093/health`=`{"status":"ok"}`. Flags intact (`GPN_FAST_CLAIM=1`, `GPN_FAST_AP=1`).
**e2e PROBE (4× POST :8092/v1/chat/completions, llama3.2:1b):** #3995 **5.68s** (>5s cap), #3996 **2.77s**, #3997 **2.47s**, #3999 **2.83s** (<5s). The **3rd probe (#3998) HUNG** — curl `-m 30` timed out with no response.
**ANOMALY + ROOT CAUSE (measured, not assumed):** on-chain `GET /jobs` shows **#3998 `Running`, provider=our addr**, and `assignments.json` **has** key 3998 — but `~/.gpn/llm_store.json` has **NO 3998 entry** (max key at read = 3997). Provider log: 6× `[provider] claiming LLM job #3998` (22:01:08–15) then **no** `running inference` — both `run_job` (fast path) and the reconcile pass gate on `get_job(id)` from the store, which was empty ⇒ the on-chain-claimed job can never run ⇒ client hangs. **Cause:** `llm_store.json` is a shared, **lock-free** JSON (only an in-process `Mutex`; **no flock** — verified in `store.rs`), and commit `5fde137` added an mtime-cached in-process map. `save()` = write-`tmp` + `rename` with **no disk re-read**, so a concurrent writer's stale map clobbers: the provider's `complete(3997)` tmp (no 3998) renamed OVER the scheduler's `put(3998)` — final file mtime **22:01:05.023** *predates* the assignment write **22:01:05.091**, i.e. the clobber won. Classic multi-process lost update between the AP (scheduler), the provider, and the heartbeat — all three share these files.
**ACTION: NONE mutating (justified).** Not a hang/deadlock (provider served #3999 fine @22:04:56) ⇒ restart would be a reflex. #3998 self-heals: the AP janitor's permissionless `expire_job` reclaims non-terminal jobs past `created_at + max_duration` (150 blocks; still `Running` at run end @22:08, reclaim pending its deadline). No code/config/flag change; fast path untouched.
**PROPOSED FIX (needs build + ordered restart — deliberate, NOT done unattended):** wrap `LlmStore` load-modify-save (and the AP/heartbeat `assignments.json` writers) in an OS advisory file lock (flock on a sidecar lockfile) so concurrent writers can't drop entries. **FLAG FOR JEREMY (medium severity, test traffic):** rare payload-loss race in the lock-free shared store strands a claimed job (this run: 1 of 4 probes); durable fix = file locking + build/ordered restart.

## 2026-10-16 11:12 PT / 18:12 UTC — PM07 GPN debug (cron 95b27deb) — **ROOT-CAUSED (not a new failure) the longstanding `healed leaked Pending` churn: a STABLE ~+70 job-id DRIFT between the AP fast path's predicted ids (which key the off-chain job store + provider dispatch) and on-chain `ComputeMarketplace::NextJobId`. No code change this run (touches the APPROVED fast path → design decision → escalate).**
**SERVICES:** 6/6 gpn units active (accesspoint/faucet/fleet/fleet-directive/provider-heartbeat/provider) + `ollama.service` active (PID 447045, NRestarts=0; keep_alive 3600s holds — `/api/ps` expires_at = now+1h). `gpn-node.service` shows inactive but the node runs under `gpn-fleet` (PID 3719827, authoring, head #143651). 0 unit ERRORs/panics, provider NRestarts=0. e2e `POST :8092/v1/chat/completions` qwen2.5:0.5b = **1.92 / 1.02 / 0.40 s** (HTTP200 coherent; well under the 5 s cap). Fast path untouched (`GPN_FAST_CLAIM=1`/`GPN_FAST_AP=1`), no flags/restarts/state touched.
**SYMPTOM THAT TRIGGERED THE DIG:** `GET /jobs` (window 4406–4661) persistently shows the trailing ids `Pending` (e.g. #4660/#4661 then #4662/#4663), and the provider logs a continuous `[provider] healed leaked Pending #<id> → Completed` churn (~88 in 60 min, each id re-logged ~every 10 s until it lands). Prior runs filed this as "documented false-Pending fast-path self-heal, not a new fault" without asking *why* the ids mismatch.
**EVIDENCE (measured this run):**
- On-chain `NextJobId` = **4664** (live; watched it advance 4662→4663→4664). `/job/{4664..4734}` = **"not found"** — no on-chain job exists for any of those ids.
- Off-chain store `~/.gpn/llm_store.json` holds keys **4650…4734**, all `status: done`, contiguous (no gaps). Max store key **4734** vs chain `NextJobId` **4664** ⇒ **offset +70**.
- The offset is **stable, not growing**: AP label vs chain-next = ~69 (Oct 15 22:34), ~69 (Oct 16 08:27), ~70 (now) — one request advances *both* counters by +1.
- Origin: the offset was introduced while the **AP hot wallet was dry / the marketplace was frozen** (fixed at Oct 15 20:40, commit `0dd9390`: "NextJobId 4305 frozen: AP hot wallet dry < price+ED"). During that window `create_job` could not land, yet the fast path still served + labelled requests (below), so the process-local predictor ran ~70 ids ahead of the chain and — because `alloc_predicted_job_id` uses `max(local, chain_next)` — never self-corrected once the wallet was topped up.
**ROOT CAUSE (decided from evidence):** `gpn-agent/src/bin/gpn_scheduler.rs` fast AP path — `alloc_predicted_job_id(next_before)` (L182) predicts the new id from a **process-local counter = max(local, chain_next)+1**, and on `create_job_fast` (L1364) the **`Ok` branch trusts pool acceptance without confirming inclusion** (only the `Err` branch at L1377 re-checks `NextJobId` and `align_alloc`s). `create_job_fast` (`chain/mod.rs`) returns as soon as the tx is accepted into the pool. So any `create_job` that is accepted but never included (dry wallet → balance check fails at inclusion, or pool eviction) leaves the predictor permanently ahead of the chain. The predicted id then keys BOTH the off-chain store (`LlmStore::put`, L1451) and the provider dispatch — and the chain creates the job under the *real* id.
**CONSEQUENCE (why the churn isn't benign):** the provider's leak-healer (`gpn_llm_provider.rs` L626–650) matches an on-chain `Pending` job **by raw id**: `get_job(id)` → if that off-chain entry is `done` it drives `accept_job → start_job → submit_result(j.result_hash) → complete_job` and logs `healed leaked Pending #id`. With a +70 drift, on-chain job J is paired with off-chain store key J — a **different request** — so every chain job is ticked to `Completed` using the **wrong request's result hash**, and the real work is only ever tracked off-chain under the drifted id. It also means ~70 requests were served with **no on-chain job / no escrow** (testnet free-AI, so no visible client-visible failure; e2e stays fast).
**ACTION: NONE mutating.** This is real but (a) longstanding/stable, (b) not breaking any service or the e2e path, and (c) any fix changes the semantics of the **APPROVED** fast path (`GPN_FAST_AP`), which the standing directive says to leave ON and not re-default. Per the review protocol this is a design decision, not a mechanical bugfix, so I did **not** touch code, flags, or the allocator. No hang/deadlock (NRestarts=0, serving) ⇒ no restart.
**PROPOSED FIX (for REVIEW/APPROVE — pick one):**
  - **A (contain, no latency cost):** after a fast `create_job_fast` Ok, reconcile the local predictor to on-chain `NextJobId` on the next request when no create is in flight (heals the drift; prevents re-accumulation after a future dry-wallet/drop). One file, off-chain, revertible. *Risk:* LOW; *Rollback:* `git revert`.
  - **B (correctness at the source):** have the leak-healer match a `Pending` chain job to an off-chain entry by **content** (prompt/`result_hash` or the AP→provider assignment token) instead of by raw id, so a drifted id can never finalize the wrong job. One file, off-chain, revertible. *Risk:* LOW–MED. *Rollback:* `git revert`.
  (A alone fixes the offset; B is the defence-in-depth so a future drift can't corrupt results. Both together preferred.)
**ESCALATION:** this finding needs Jeremy/a design call (fast-path prediction semantics). Recommend A+B as one small PR after approval. STATUS: **GREEN (services + e2e), but OPEN ANOMALY logged (id drift → wrong-hash leak-heal).**

## 2026-10-16 16:52 PT / 23:52 UTC — **NEW QUEUE ITEM #28 DONE: cross-process lost-update on the shared off-chain stores (the #4858 dropped-payload class) — ROOT-CAUSED + FIXED + LIVE-DEPLOYED (off-chain; no genesis/runtime).**
**WHAT:** `gpn_agent::llm::store::LlmStore` (the AP/provider/heartbeat-shared `~/.gpn/llm_store.json`) and the two `write_assignment` copies (`gpn_scheduler.rs` + `gpn_provider_status.rs`, shared `~/.gpn/assignments.json`) did a **lock-free read-modify-write of the WHOLE json file across processes** — only a per-process `Mutex` (+ an mtime cache), no OS lock. A process holding a stale map renamed its tmp over another process's insert ⇒ **lost update** (verified 2026-10-16 16:31: the AP's `LlmStore::put(4858)` was clobbered by an unrelated provider `complete()`, so the provider never had the payload ⇒ 40 no-op claims ⇒ AP blocked ~360 s, client 60 s timeout).
**FIX (ONE class, smallest correct change; std-only, no new deps; builds Linux + Windows):** new **`gpn_agent::llm::StoreLock`** — a portable cross-process advisory lock using an atomic lock-**directory** (`create_dir` is atomic on every OS; stale lock broken after 30 s; bounded 10 s wait so the AP can never deadlock) — plus **`merge_json_object()`**. All `LlmStore` mutators (`put`/`set_status`/`complete`/`complete_artifact`/`set_error`) now acquire the lock and re-read the file **fresh** (`load_fresh()`, bypassing the process cache) before writing; both `write_assignment` copies call `merge_json_object()`. `get()` fast path, `load()`, cache, and all public write semantics unchanged.
**TESTS:** +3 (`store_lock_is_mutually_exclusive`; `merge_json_object_preserves_existing_keys`; `concurrent_puts_do_not_lose_entries` — two independent handles writing the same file, the lost-update case). `cargo test --release --lib llm::store` = **5/5 green**; `gpn_llm_provider`/`gpn_scheduler`/`gpn_provider_status` release build clean.
**DEPLOY (rule 5a):** new bins installed to `~/.local/bin` (temp+mv; `.bak-<ts>` kept) → `systemctl --user restart gpn-accesspoint gpn-provider gpn-provider-heartbeat` (all active; provider log `fast claim path: ON`, ollama warm). **VERIFIED:** e2e `POST :8092/v1/chat/completions` qwen2.5:0.5b ×3 = **0.56 / 0.66 / 0.67 s HTTP 200** coherent (was 1 of 3 timing out); `~/.gpn/llm_store.json` + `assignments.json` both advance together, no `*.lockdir` debris left.
**RISK/ROLLBACK (per protocol):** LOW — off-chain; no chain/genesis/runtime/`set_code`; critical sections ~ms; fully revertible (`git revert` + `systemctl --user restart gpn-provider gpn-accesspoint gpn-provider-heartbeat`). **RESIDUAL (separate, still escalated — NOT this item):** the AP fast-path **+~70 id drift** (predicted label vs on-chain `NextJobId`; reconcile-after-Ok + content-keyed leak-heal, proposal A+B awaiting a design call) and the host DNS/resolver defect — both pre-existing and unchanged. Queue item #28 added to `shared/artifacts/project7/GPN-TASKS.md`.

## 2026-10-16 22:32 PT / 2026-10-17 05:32 UTC — PM07 GPN debug (cron 1a4f19ab) — ROOT-CAUSED + FIXED the 1014 `Priority is too low` claim storm (nonce re-seed behind pool after stream drop); e2e healthy (0.98–1.31 s)
**CHECKS:** journal showed a real storm: `pipelined claim #4945 failed` **10× in 5 s** with an unchanging pair `Priority is too low: (2729 vs 2613)`, plus one reconcile `#4941` rejection and two `heal #4947` submits that sat >60 s before inclusion. e2e probes: **1.31 s / 0.98 s HTTP 200**, 793/703 chars (~180–200 tok/s). `/jobs` had #4947/#4948 Pending during block gaps, both healed to Accepted/Completed on their own → **not orphans**; claim count 1 per request.
**ROOT CAUSE (evidence):** the collisions all started within seconds of the 22:23:07 restart and stopped once blocks caught up. `NonceStream::new` seeds `next_nonce` from **current_nonce(head block)**, which excludes txs still in the **pool** from the previous process. A failed submit drops the stream (`mod.rs` Err arm), so every retry re-seeds from the same stale head nonce and re-collides — the same nonce, same 1014, forever until inclusion. The two priorities (2729 vs 2613) are two different call sizes (accept vs start/completion), i.e. our own two tx types fighting for one nonce.
**FIX (one file, off-chain, provider only):** `NonceStream::submit` now retries a **nonce collision** by stepping the local counter forward (bounded, 8 attempts), mirroring the existing `submit_signed` rule, instead of returning Err into the drop/re-seed loop. Happy path unchanged; no flag, fast-path, or nonce-stream ownership change.
**VERIFY:** release build clean (2m34s), `.bak` retained, provider restarted 22:30:49 → advert ok, `fast claim path: ON` + infer server up in 11 s; **0 collision/1014 lines in the 3 min since** (was 11 in 12 min pre-fix); #4952 Accepted, e2e 2/2 fast and coherent.
**STILL OPEN (unchanged, escalated, infra):** single-peer ban loop (105 bans/2h) causing 40–70 s block-import gaps; drift A+B decision. No flags/defaults touched.
**STATUS: GREEN serving; 1014 storm root-caused and fixed.**

**Finding (class: off-chain efficiency / duplicate extrinsics):** `heal_attempt_allowed` allowed a retry once `head > last_head`. The head advances on essentially every ordinary block — usually filled with other people's extrinsics — while our heal tx can still be queued, so the gate degenerated to the wall-clock behaviour #33 was meant to replace. Measured since the #33 deploy: **12 heal lines for 10 (job,step) pairs (16.7% wasted)**; #5027 `started (Accepted)` at 02:58:38 **and** 02:59:29 (our start was submitted the same second fleet prepared a block whose slot went to another job's accept; it only landed with the next block, 02:59:40) and #5029 `accept` at 03:08:24 / 03:09:15. All-day baseline 21.6% → no measurable improvement.
**Fix (smallest correct change; provider + chain client only):** gate on **inclusion of our own tx**, not on head movement. `submit_fast` now delegates to `submit_fast_nonce` and returns the nonce the tx was signed with; new `accept/start/submit_result/complete_job_fast_nonce` wrappers thread it out of the heal path (every other caller keeps the unchanged `Result<()>` API). The gate stores `(Instant, Option<u64>)` and retries only when `account_nonce_at_head(me)` is **strictly greater** than the submitted nonce (nonces are ordered and never skipped ⇒ exact proof the tx was applied; unreadable ⇒ never evidence) **or** `HEAL_RETRY_FLOOR` (120 s) has elapsed (liveness for a genuinely dropped tx). A **rejected** submit clears its gate entry so the next reconcile pass may retry at once.
**Tests:** +1 `retry_waits_for_our_own_nonce_not_for_the_head` (landed / not-landed / unreadable / floor matrix, backdated entries) and 3 rewritten — `cargo test --release --bin gpn_llm_provider` **10/10 green**; all release bins build clean (3 pre-existing warnings).

**SERVICES:** 9 gpn units as expected — accesspoint, provider, provider-heartbeat, fleet, fleet-directive, faucet, ap-topup(+timer) active; `gpn-node`/`explorer`/`diffusion`/`finetune` inactive *by design* (fleet supervisor hosts the node; GPU services off). `gpn-ap-topup` "activating" at first look was only a mid-run 5-min timer tick (finished status=0/SUCCESS).

**ANOMALY (verified, low severity but a real logic bug):** the #38 adopt loop fires on **almost every job** — 8 false "adopted untracked #N … created in-flight across an AP restart" lines in 55 min (#5509, #5511, #5512, #5514, #5515, #5516, #5517, #5519) although the AP never restarted after 16:52. All 8 were healthy jobs that completed normally. `POST /jobs` shows 254+ Completed and 0 stranded.
**ROOT CAUSE (measured, not inferred):** with `GPN_FAST_AP=1` a create is **pool-ack only**. Measured directly on `#5521`: `Jobs[5521]` did **not exist on chain for >36 s** after the HTTP 200 (block interval in this window ≫ median 11 s; pool backlog). The janitor reconcile loop runs every 30 s and does `let Some((state,..)) = get_job_state(id) else { continue; }` — i.e. it treats **"storage item absent because the create is still in the pool"** identically to "job gone / transient read failure" — and silently drops the job from `recent_jobs()`. The #38 trailing-window scan then sees a non-terminal job of ours that isn't tracked and re-adds it via `record_created(id, 0)`. **Consequence:** the token-scaled stale window (`60 s + max_tokens/20 × 2`, clamped 120–900 s) is destroyed for essentially every job and collapses to the 120 s floor; any job with `max_tokens ≳ 1200` (stale window 180 s+) can now be requestor-**cancelled by our own janitor while it is legitimately in flight**. No such cancellation has happened yet (only the genuine orphans #5503/#5504 were cancelled), but the path is live. The log message is also wrong (no restart occurred), which is why this looked like restart noise.
**PROPOSED FIX (WHAT; smallest correct change, off-chain scheduler only — no genesis, no runtime, no flags):** in the reconcile loop, distinguish "absent because not yet included / transient read" from "gone": if `get_job_state` returns `None`, **keep** the entry (preserving the real `max_tokens`) while `now - t <= JANITOR_MAX_SECS + 120 s` grace, and only drop it once it has aged past that (a job that never lands still ages out and frees the slot, so no leak). The #38 adopt scan stays as the restart-recovery net but will no longer fire in steady state.
**WHY:** a missing storage item is not evidence of a dead job when our own create is still in the pool — the fast path guarantees a window of exactly this, and the janitor's 30 s period is shorter than the observed create→inclusion latency. Preserving `max_tokens` restores the intended token scaling and removes the premature-cancel exposure.
**RISK:** LOW — tracking-list membership only; reclaim actions (`cancel_job`/`expire_job`) are unchanged and still gated by the same deadlines. Worst case a genuinely dead job stays tracked ~120 s longer and is then dropped (it would already be past its on-chain deadline, where `expire_job` reclaims it).
**ROLLBACK:** `git revert <sha>` + `systemctl --user restart gpn-accesspoint` (binary `.bak` retained).
**TESTS PLAN:** extend the janitor unit test: (a) entry younger than grace with unreadable state survives a pass, (b) entry older than grace with unreadable state is dropped, (c) a healthy job's `max_tokens` survives several passes.

- 18:58:20 provider `claiming LLM job #5534`; 18:58:21 `[job 5534] result returned to AP` / `done — response 524 chars`.
- 18:59:50 provider `heal #5534: accept submitted (Pending)`; 19:00:51 `started (Accepted)`; 19:01:01 `result submitted (Running)` — i.e. **the on-chain transitions lagged ~90 s behind the actual work**, because our accept/start txs sat in the pool while blocks were sparse (~61 s apart).

- 19:01:05 `[janitor] adopted untracked #5534 (Running) — created in-flight across an AP restart` — the bogus-adopt symptom of #38/#39 reappeared *because the cancel path itself drops the tracking entry on successful submit* (`continue`), after which the adopt scan re-adds it with `max_tokens 0`.
**ROOT CAUSE:** the fast-path cancel criterion is `state == Pending && age > stale_secs(max_tokens)`. It has **no knowledge of provider progress**: the AP itself stored the provider's result (`LlmStore` status `done`) at 18:58:21, yet the chain still said Pending until the queued accept/start landed. `stale_secs` floors at 120 s, while observed block cadence (and therefore accept/start inclusion) is currently 60–120 s per transition ⇒ the floor can expire while a served job is still mid-finalisation. The dropped-tracking + re-adopt with `max_tokens 0` is the same #38/#39 mechanism, now reached via the cancel path rather than an absent read.
**PROPOSED FIX (WHAT; smallest correct change; off-chain scheduler only — no genesis, no runtime, no flags):**
1. Before issuing a requestor cancel, skip it when the AP already holds a provider result for that id — `gpn_agent::llm::get_job(id)` with `status` in {`done`, `error`} (persisted, so it also survives an AP restart). Such a job is left to the normal completion path, and to the pallet `expire_job` reclaim past its on-chain deadline if completion never lands.
2. On a successful cancel **submit**, keep the tracking entry (reset its retry clock) instead of dropping it, so the adopt scan cannot re-add the id with `max_tokens 0`; a retry is still naturally throttled by the same `stale_secs` window, and the entry disappears when the state becomes terminal.
**WHY:** "work already delivered" is strictly stronger evidence than an age heuristic; cancelling a delivered job can only lose the provider's payment or burn a rejected tx. The fix preserves the janitor's real purpose (reclaim genuinely stranded Pending jobs) and its token-scaled window.
**RISK:** LOW — adds one local store read per stale-tracked job per 30 s pass; cancel/expire transitions and nonce handling unchanged. Worst case: a job that got a provider result but never completes stays tracked until `expire_job` / the absent-read grace ages it out (no slot leak; `expire_job` still reclaims at the on-chain deadline).
**ROLLBACK:** `git revert <sha>` + `systemctl --user restart gpn-accesspoint` (binary `.bak` retained).
**TESTS PLAN:** unit tests for the status predicate ({queued,running}→cancel allowed; {done,error}→skipped); `cargo test --release --bin gpn_scheduler`; build clean.

2. **The claim burst reverted on-chain.** Block **165370** carries 3 provider-signed `ComputeMarketplace` extrinsics whose payload ends in job id **5994** (accept, start, submit_result) *plus* the requestor's `create_job` for the same block (`Jobs[5994]` `created_at` = 165370). The job did not exist on chain when accept/start were dispatched, so all three reverted (nonce consumed, no state change); the txpool is empty and the job never left `Pending`. 3. **Reconcile is silent.** The pass that exists for exactly this case (`heal_step_for_state("Pending") = Accept`, store entry `status=done` + `result_hash` present, id inside `RECONCILE_WINDOW` 128) printed **nothing** in 4 min of observation; the only heal lines in the whole last hour are 15:05–15:14. **ROOT CAUSE (established):** the fast-path claim is submitted on the *AP's off-chain lease*, deliberately before the `create_job` is included ("claim optimistically so we serve the client fast", `gpn_llm_provider.rs:1200-1224`). On a slow chain (this run: 25–50 s/block, create included 94 s after the request) the accept/start/submit_result all execute in the same block as the create *ahead of it*, i.e. `JobNotFound` → revert. With one pass of output the silent branch is identified and the real fix (bounded retry that treats "included but state unchanged" as a revert, which the gate already supports) can be targeted. Alternative/parallel: make the fast-path claim wait for `create_job` inclusion only when `get_job_state` is `None` for a *known* id, i.e. drop the optimistic claim that produces the reverts in the first place.

Same #49/#52 class as #8–#36, no tx loss. Cadence recovered at once (172570–172578 in 11–15 s each).

**NEW DEFECT FOUND + ROOT-CAUSED (evidence, then proposal — no code touched):** `gpn_diffusion_provider` (pid 1353412) held **91 % CPU for 10.4 h** (main thread utime 3.25 M ticks = 32,457 s) while holding **0 MiB** GPU and serving nothing. Measured evidence: main-thread `rchar` **1.27 TB total ≈ 34 MB/s sustained**, `syscr` **8.8 k reads/s**, 95 % **user** (not I/O wait), and `/proc/*/io` shows the read traffic is on the **main thread only**. Source: `gpn-agent/src/bin/gpn_diffusion_provider.rs:388` calls `client.list_claimable_jobs()` **unconditionally every cycle**, and `chain/mod.rs:1648` implements it as `for id in 0..next { storage_at_head(Jobs[id]) }` — **one `state_getStorage` RPC per job id**. With `NextJobId` = 6,371 that is **≈6,371 sequential RPCs per 2 s poll** (≈32 s of CPU per cycle at ~5 ms/RPC incl. scale decode — self-consistent with 1,063 cycles in 10.4 h at 95 %). The result is then **thrown away**: every id is filtered by `is_gen()` and all of them are `llm`, so nothing is ever claimed. (`gpn_llm_provider` avoids this because line ~1709 only calls `list_claimable_jobs` when `assigned.is_empty()`; it still sits at 43 % CPU.) Secondary contributor in the same loop: the `RECONCILE_WINDOW=128` sweep does 128 more RPCs per cycle.
**WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND WASTE:** this process alone issues ~3,000 RPC/s against the node that is also the sole GPU sealer, on a 12-core box with load 3.7 — a credible contributor to the bimodal 37–120 s local seal times that gate e2e (#52 class, now 37 recurrences). It also pulls and stores every LLM job it can never serve (shared signer + `caps_snapshot()` reading the LLM heartbeat :8093, so the AP legitimately believes this identity serves `llama3.2:1b`).
**PROPOSAL (CHANGE = REVIEW FIRST — awaiting MAIN APPROVE; not applied):**
- WHAT: in `gpn_diffusion_provider` only — (1) throttle the claimable scan to once per `GPN_CLAIM_SCAN_MS` (default 30 000) and bound it to the most recent `GPN_CLAIM_SCAN_WINDOW` ids (default 512) via a new `list_claimable_jobs_window(from, to, gflops)` that `list_claimable_jobs` then delegates to (no behaviour change for the other three callers); (2) throttle the `AwaitingVerification`/`Accepted` reconcile sweep to once per `GPN_RECONCILE_MS` (default 30 000). No genesis, no runtime, no `set_code`, no env/flag change.
- WHY: removes ~6,371 → ≤512 RPCs per 30 s from a process that produces nothing, off the node that must seal blocks; expected CPU 91 % → low single digits.
- RISK: a gen job older than the window (≈512 ids ≈ 1–2 h of jobs at current rates) would no longer be self-claimed; it is expiry-swept anyway. Throttled reconcile means a stranded `AwaitingVerification` job can hold a capacity slot up to 30 s longer — it already sits for a full poll cycle (≈32 s) today, so no regression.
- ROLLBACK: revert the one commit (two constants + one helper); no state, no config, no on-chain effect.
**ACTION THIS RUN:** none — no code change, no restart (nothing dead/hung), no flag/env change, no state wipe. Proposal written here because `sessions_list` shows **only this cron session** (no MAIN reviewer to send the REVIEW REQUEST to) ⇒ needs Jeremy or a MAIN session to approve before it can be implemented.
**ESCALATION (unchanged, needs Jeremy — 37th recurrence):** <5 s e2e stays unreachable behind the #49 create-inclusion gate: (a) accept a 30–60 s SLO / shorten block time, (b) item #8 pallet-side optimistic-claim expire/timeout, (c) #52 clamp/window widening (40–60). Adding: (d) approve the diffusion-provider RPC-burn fix above — it is the only change on the board that removes *local* contention from the sealer path.
